gloss: An immanent form of knowledge or transcendent insight, such as sought by the Gnostics.
The act or process of knowing in general.
An altered state of awareness in which the will is magically effective.
To bite something persistently, especially something tough.
To produce excessive anxiety or worry.
To corrode; to fret away; to waste.
To grind (one's teeth) in pain or in anger.
To grind between the teeth.
To clash together violently.
To run away.
A large antelope of the genus Connochaetes, native to Africa, having curved horns.
An elemental (spirit or corporeal creature associated with a classical element) associated with earth.

One of a race of imaginary human-like beings, usually depicted as short and typically bearded males, who inhabit the inner parts of the earth and act as guardians of mines, mineral treasure, etc.; in modern fantasy literature and games, when distinguished from dwarves, gnomes are usually smaller than dwarves and more focused on engineering than mining.
A person of a small stature or misshapen features, or of a strange appearance.
The mountain pygmy owl, Glaucidium gnoma, a small owl of the western United States.
An object such as a pillar or a rod that is used to tell time by the shadow it casts when the sun shines on it, especially the pointer on a sundial.

An object such as a pillar used by an observer to calculate the meridian altitude of the sun (that is, the altitude of the sun when it reaches the observer's meridian), for the purpose of determining the observer's latitude.
The index of the hour circle of a globe.
A plane figure formed by removing a parallelogram from a corner of a larger parallelogram.
A biting insect, especially a mosquito.
An annoying person.
A knot in wood; a knurl or a protuberance with twisted grain, on a tree.
Something resembling a knot in wood, such as in stone or limbs.
Of, or relating to gnomes (sententious sayings).
Mysterious and often incomprehensible yet seemingly wise.
Expressing general truths or aphorisms.
Italian pasta-like dumpling(s) made of potato or semolina.

A wide variety of Jewish and early Christian sects having an interest in gnosis, or divine knowledge, and generally holding the belief that there is a god greater than the Demiurge, or the creator of the world.
Knotty and misshapen.
Made rough by age or hard work.
A common and widely-distributed metamorphic rock having bands or veins, but not schistose.
The philosophical study of knowledge.
of or relating to gneiss
The science, art and craft of designing and constructing sundials.
Of or pertaining to gnoseology, the study of knowledge.
Showing all great circles as straight lines, and thus preserving the shortest distances between any two locations.
One skilled in gnomonics; a person who makes sundials.
A city in Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland.
